## Narrative

The most strongly enriched pathway in this dataset is **Eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167; FDR ≈ 0, fold-enrichment ≈ 1001), populated by five of the ten differentially-abundant metabolites: arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717), and 5-HETE (C04805). A second highly enriched node, the **Selenium micronutrient network** (WP15; FDR ≈ 0, fold-enrichment ≈ 292), links arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, hypochlorite (C19697), and copper (C00070), suggesting a broader oxidative-inflammatory context beyond classical eicosanoid chemistry.

**Key drivers.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) occupies the upstream apex of the eicosanoid cascade. KEGG graph traversal confirms it is connected to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via a two-reaction path through 5-HPETE (C05356), establishing arachidonic acid as the canonical precursor. The detected 5-HETE (C04805) and 15-HETE (C04742) represent the two major lipoxygenase branches (5-LOX and 15-LOX, respectively), while 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717) reflects cyclopentenone prostaglandin signaling with known anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving activity. Histamine (C00388), while not part of the eicosanoid core pathway, can synergize with LOX products to amplify vascular permeability and leukocyte recruitment.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of arachidonic acid alongside multiple downstream eicosanoids is characteristic of activated phospholipase A₂ and intensified cyclooxygenase / lipoxygenase flux — a hallmark of acute or chronic inflammatory stimulation. The concurrent presence of 15d-PGJ₂ is particularly noteworthy: this cyclopentenone prostaglandin can activate Nrf2 and suppress NF-κB, indicating the system may be engaged in a resolving-phase response. Hypochlorite and copper dysregulation (both in the selenium micronutrient network) suggest metal-dependent redox stress, potentially amplifying oxidative modification of membrane lipids and contributing to the eicosanoid surge.

In summary, the data point to a robust inflammatory eicosanoid response anchored by arachidonic acid, with multi-axis LOX product formation and an accompanying anti-inflammatory prostaglandin signal — consistent with active inflammation transitioning toward resolution.
